candidates.title: The Killings: Parrish Station
candidates.reason: A complete six-episode dual-timeline murder mystery whose structure strongly matches the profile: Georgia Cooke investigates the 1987 massacre and, decades later, copycat killings reopen the case. The episode progression supplies meaningful information throughout rather than reserving everything for the finale: the Bone Gospel is established as real, a present-day podcaster body extends the copycat case, an older similar case is uncovered, evidence links the murder mysteries, the ritual and signal become concrete, and the penultimate episode identifies that the killer has been close to the investigators before the finale becomes a race to stop Callum Parrish. The Guardian independently characterizes the series as a murder mystery packed with twists and outlandish momentum. The main weakness is that the occult/cosmic-horror explanation makes the clue chain less grounded than a conventional procedural, and interpersonal estrangement/obsession adds a substantial drama layer, but the complete-season evidence supports frequent progressive answers, active investigation, mystery, culprit pursuit and sustained suspense.

research_rejections.title: Winter
research_rejections.reason: Qualitative rejection for now: the ITV crime series only premiered on September 30, 2026 and is releasing as an ongoing series. Current evidence establishes a forensic procedural with an overarching cold-case thread around Simone's murder, but not the complete-season revelation cadence required to measure all Thriller DNA dimensions honestly. Reconsider after the full season has aired.

research_rejections.title: Line of Fire
research_rejections.reason: Qualitative rejection for now: season one is a ten-episode weekly release that began September 21, 2026, so complete-season evidence is unavailable. Available reporting describes a conspiracy and cliffhangers but also explicitly frames the show as a family drama/procedural hybrid. Without the full season, progressive revelation and revelation frequency cannot be measured across the complete runtime without inference.

research_rejections.title: Psycho Killer
research_rejections.reason: Qualitative rejection: the 91-minute film has a police pursuit, serial-killer hunt, occult clues and brutality, but whole-film critical evidence is strongly unfavorable and specifically describes the plot as obvious with no surprises. The identity and hunt are clear, but available evidence does not support the profile's required high-confidence measurements of progressive revelation and revelation frequency as a strong fit; do not turn a serial-killer pursuit premise into assumed revelation cadence.
